question.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ as a function of $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2cos)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}=\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩=⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0 \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -3\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =(-6{cos}^{2}⁡t-6{sin}^{2}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-6\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=6.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(4{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
